entry_points.text: Standard ELF loader publishes its format descriptor on init with success and withdraws it on exit, gating loader availability.
FDPIC ELF publishes and withdraws its own format descriptor, using binary loading for recognition with core dumping and page sized granularity when supported.
Exec stack completion transfers staged argument pages downward onto the user stack, then publishes aux vectors, env and arg pointer arrays plus count, asserting the final pointer.
FDPIC core dump consumes dump parameters and reports whether header preparation completed, producing header plus descriptors plus notes plus memory images.
Flat loader registers its format object binding the module to the flat binary load callback.

exports.text: Dump output offers hole declaration and user range transfer. Holes flush before writes under a written limit with interruption checks; ranges walk page by page emitting present pages and absent pages as sparse holes.
Binary format management publishes descriptors as non prioritized entries and withdraws them under write exclusion on the shared format list.
Loader reads use a small helper that reads a file range and refreshes instruction visibility, on the generic validated dispatch to direct or vectored operations.

hazards.text: Dump failures include scratch alloc failure, hole flush failure, limit overrun, interruption, copy failure and short writes; killed lock acquisition aborts. FDPIC errors converge to one exit freeing threads and headers, with a warning on final offset mismatch.

Load failures include header size mismatch, excessive count, alloc and IO errors, bad interpreter paths, interpreter access faults, replacement and mapping errors, empty or misaligned dynamic sections and tail mismatches; only the first interpreter directive applies.
Stack construction faults on any user write failure and rejects empty or overlong arg or env strings; arg transfer aborts on copy fault leaving the caller pointer unchanged.

Flat validation failures return before teardown; mapping and content errors unmap with zero or error treated as no memory. Gunzip fails on alloc, header, bounds, init or negative inflate status, always releasing workspace, chunk and inflate state.

invariants.text: ELF core totals add area count plus arch extras plus one notes entry, saturating the header count with overflow in a section extension. Layout is header, headers, notes, aligned data, optional extension; areas map as load segments with dumped file extent and full memory span.

FDPIC acceptance needs ELF magic, executable or shared type, arch approval and mappability; managed builds require the FDPIC marker. Header tables validate entry size and a total bound; displacement is constant when the marker is missing or explicitly set.

Page output flushes pending holes only on success, enforces limits and interruption checks, then advances by a full page. Scratch has a copying variant with tolerant copy and a passthrough variant that fails allocation and returns the source.
Architecture core extensions default to neutral: no extra headers or size, and succeeding no-op writers for extra headers, data and notes.

FDPIC stack setup aligns the pointer, places load maps, reserves aux plus env plus args space, validates strings as non empty and bounded, null terminates tables, records boundaries, publishes the stack address and rebases the executable offset.

Reads require readable mode and capability, accessible destination and in range request, truncate oversized counts, fail without operations, and on success notify access with accounting. Sync vectored reads bind a user iterator at the position and write back the advance with no async queuing.

FDPIC mapping counts load entries, versions a sized load map, translates entry and header and dynamic addresses via containing segments, merges adjacent same displacement segments on paged builds, and supports const displacement reservation plus per entry direct mmap with tail provisioning.

Notes encode header plus padded name plus padded payload with mnemonic binding. Core headers carry ELF identity, core type and FDPIC flags; note headers carry offsets with 4 byte alignment. Status snapshots signals, ids, times, state and credentials; large counts use a trailing null section extension.

FDPIC core files cap the transmitted header count with overflow preserved separately, order notes as first thread primary then process info then aux vector then remaining notes, scan aux pairs for the terminator, and describe areas as load segments with zero physical address and flag derived protections.

Flat relocation rejects offsets beyond text plus data with a signal; valid offsets map into text or data bases. Old style entries add code, data or end bases with a warning on unknown types; GOT skip and relocate address handling are arch conditional with identity default.

locks.text: Format removal holds the global format write lock across list detachment to exclude concurrent mutation and traversal.
Range dumping takes the address space read lock lazily in killable mode only around page inspection, releasing before IO and rescheduling. Parent and credential reads use short RCU critical sections.

state_machines.text: FDPIC loading runs validation, interpreter resolution, stack policy, irreversible replacement, mapping, stack and table build, then thread launch. Pre replacement failures unwind; post replacement failures still report errors though the old image is gone.
ELF dumping reports note setup outcome, not full IO success. A marker sets once notes are ready and persists through output; note state and temp headers release on all exits.

FDPIC dump and map orchestration counts headers from areas plus arch extras plus notes, lays out header then descriptors then notes then aligned data, emits in order with arch extras and optional extended numbering, collects per thread notes with float detection, and frees temporaries.

Flat loading validates magic, revision, widths and limits, starts new execution, chooses ROM plus RAM or unified mapping, reads or gunzips content with workspace checks and incremental inflate, records boundaries and entry, builds aligned stack tables, and unmaps on failure.

structs.text: FDPIC format holds ownership with load and core ops plus granularity. Addresses alias mutable bytes; diagnostics are empty. Base defaults null with Linux personality; core files use core type with FDPIC flags and note headers with 4 byte alignment.

FDPIC status note is common header plus registers plus executable and interpreter map addresses plus float validity. In memory notes hold name, type, size and pointer with rounded sizing; per thread state links status, float image and up to two notes.

Flat library table has one slot with code, data, break, lengths, entry, date and loaded flag. Data align 32; chunk 4000; reloc fail 0xff00ff01; unloaded 0x7ff000ff; max libs 1; gzip flags 0x01 0x02 0x04 0x08 0x10 0x20 0xC0; offset words and count update are 0 or lib limit by config.

ELF FDPIC ABI: saturation at PN_XNUM 0xffff; align by EXEC_PAGESIZE; areas PT_LOAD with PF_R/W/X from protections and cleared paddr. Magic ELFMAG/SELFMAG; ET_EXEC/ET_DYN; PT_GNU_STACK with enable/disable/default; default stack 131072; table cap 65536; aux base DLINFO_ITEMS 15 with 8/16 byte alignment; FDPIC present/executable/constdisp/exec/noexec flags.
